prev_agent: That confirms it — and it rules out the DOM scrape (and my H1 change) as the cause. **Why:** the normal roster with toggles is rendered from `data.roster`, which comes **only** from the engine's draft (`useDraft` → `DRAFT_LOAD`). The DOM snapshot's scraped emails never reach that roster — they only appear on the pre-save "Save the event…" notice. So `j765894110@gmail.com` is **engine-draft-sourced**, not scraped from the page. That leaves two sub-causes, and they need different fixes: 1. **Stale persisted draft** — the engine keeps a guest keyed by `iCalUid` even after it's removed from the calendar event (its reconcile is deliberately conservative; the panel even comments on it). A previous session seeded that address and it's been sticking around. → **a data wipe clears it and it won't come back.** 2. **Live Calendar API attendee** — the event genuinely still carries `j765894110@gmail.com` per Google's API (a declined guest, a group-expanded invite, or a Google-internal pseudo-address), even though the UI shows "no guests." `fetchActiveEvent` forwards it to the engine each open. → **a wipe won't help; it reappears on next open, and the fix is to filter/understand it.** The address itself (`j` + 9 digits `@gmail.com`) looks auto-generated, which mildly favors #2 — but it's not conclusive. **The wipe is the right next step, but it only tells you the answer if you capture the API response first.** If you wipe and it's gone, you can't tell whether it was stale data (#1, fixed) or just not-yet-reloaded (#2, will return). So I'd suggest one cheap, dev-only diagnostic before the test: a `DEBUG`-gated log in `fetchActiveEvent` that prints the **actual attendee emails Google returns** (not just the count it logs today). Then, running `npm run dev` and opening the event: - phantom **in the API log** → it's a real API attendee …
